requirements.title: Named scalar Fortran variables are interoperable under scalar eligibility conditions
requirements.definition: A named scalar Fortran variable is interoperable exactly with interoperable type and type parameters, non-coarray status, absence of ALLOCATABLE and POINTER, and constant nonassumed character length for character variables.

pending.scalar-variable-type-parameters-interope: Positive mixed plan declares INTEGER(C_INT), REAL(C_DOUBLE), and CHARACTER(KIND=C_CHAR,LEN=1) scalar BIND(C) variables initialized to sentinels; C writes exact 64, -8.0, and R, then Fortran verifies exact changed values.
pending.scalar-variable-not-coarray: Out of scope by user decision: observing coarray exclusion requires coarray/image semantics beyond the single-image packet scope. Future single-image fixtures must not claim scalar coarray interoperability.
pending.scalar-variable-not-allocatable: Source-control plan contrasts INTEGER(C_INT), BIND(C) :: x with an ALLOCATABLE scalar variant and records the latter as non-interoperable; no diagnostic is required by this unnumbered definition.
pending.scalar-variable-not-pointer: Source-control plan contrasts INTEGER(C_INT), BIND(C) :: x with a POINTER scalar variant and records the latter as non-interoperable; no diagnostic is required by this unnumbered definition.
pending.scalar-character-length-constant-not-ass: Positive mixed plan uses CHARACTER(KIND=C_CHAR,LEN=1) and C char with sentinel X changed to T. Source-control variants with assumed length or nonconstant length are retained as non-interoperable without diagnostic credit here.

requirements.oracle: Source registration only. Positive plans establish load-bearing values before the observation, usually with distinct sentinels or C-written data, then assert only portable properties: successful compilation and linking, exact integer/logical/character values, exactly representable real values, required rejection of numbered constraints, or source-use restrictions fixed by the standard. Mixed Fortran/C plans build a Fortran source with a small C companion. They do not assert kind numbers, addresses, structure padding, diagnostic wording, C implementation details beyond the declared companion objects, or support for a C type whose ISO_C_BINDING named constant is negative.
requirements.oracle_limitation: This packet creates no Fortran fixture, compiler invocation, execution evidence, evidence link, fixture approval, oracle approval, or coverage claim. Unnumbered program restrictions are retained as source-control plans and are not promoted to required diagnostic facets. Coarray-dependent observations are out of scope by user decision. NOTES and examples are informative only.
requirements.dependencies: Registered dependencies: clauses 6, 7, 8, 10, 11, 12, 13, 15, and 16 for source form, types, attributes, expressions, execution, I/O, procedure calls, and ISO_C_BINDING named constants and procedures. Unregistered or separately catalogued dependencies explicitly retained: C companion semantics from ISO/IEC 9899:2018, BIND(C) data-entity rules, ENUM definitions, argument association, 18.3.7 procedure interoperability, 18.10 ISO_C_BINDING procedures, and later C descriptor rules.

requirements.title: Interoperable scalar Fortran variables interoperate with scalar C entities by type and parameters
requirements.definition: An interoperable scalar Fortran variable is interoperable with a scalar C entity exactly through interoperable types and type parameters.

pending.scalar-fortran-variable-c-entity-type-ma: Mixed global plan declares a C int object and a Fortran INTEGER(C_INT), BIND(C, NAME="shared_value") scalar initialized through Fortran to -777; C sets shared_value to 246 and Fortran verifies exact 246.
pending.scalar-c-entity-round-trip-values: Mixed plan uses C functions to set and read INTEGER(C_INT), REAL(C_DOUBLE) exact 3.5, LOGICAL(C_BOOL), and CHARACTER(C_CHAR) scalars; Fortran initializes distinct sentinels first and checks exact final values.

review_rationale: Source registration for 18.3 and 18.3.1-18.3.6: interoperability of intrinsic types, C pointer types, derived types and C structures, and scalar and array variables (batch242). Every unit hash-verified by an independent reviewer across two rounds; C1801-C1806 had no existing tests, and every correspondence is planned as a mixed Fortran/C program with hand-derived values. 18.3.7 (already on main) is untouched. Source accounting only.
